welcome.label: Welcome · prove it to the council

parts.label: 📝 Councilor Ruiz’s note
parts.title: Prove It to the Council
parts.body: “No money for a lightning rod unless you PROVE energy moves, with evidence I can check myself.”

parts.label: 🔎 The case question
parts.title: What evidence will convince her?
parts.body: Today we collect evidence she can check.

welcome.script:
(Hold up a mug.) This mug is warm. Trust me! … Do you believe me? Why not?

[ON SCREEN: Councilor Ruiz’s note]
Councilor Ruiz doesn’t believe Sam’s readings from the storm. She wants evidence she can check herself.

[ON SCREEN: The case question]
Let’s give her some. Press Listen on Sam’s walkie-talkie, right below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · convince the doubter (Clue 1)
warmup.script:
(Raise one eyebrow like a doubter.) I’m a doubter today. Convince me!

[ON SCREEN: Prove it!]
Which one would convince YOU? Show me one finger, two or three. Most of you picked the number. Why? Because you could check it yourself. Now convince Councilor Ruiz. Press Listen.

part1.label: Part 1 · build-a-station kit (Clue 2)
part1.script:
(Hold up a flashlight, then a sheet of paper, then a ruler.) Source… receiver… and a tool to measure.

[ON SCREEN: Every station needs]
Build all four stations. Careful: two parts don’t belong anywhere. Press Listen.

part2.label: Part 2 · hands lie, numbers don’t (Clue 3)
part2.script:
[ON SCREEN: The three bowls]
With an adult, you can try this at home with warm tap water. One hand warm, one hand cold, then both in the middle. Your hands will argue! Press Listen.

explore.label: Part 4 · run the stations (Clue 4)
explore.script:
(Squint at a ruler, then tap a number with your finger.) Scientists don’t guess. They read the tool.

[ON SCREEN: Run all four]
Run each station twice, then tap the number the tool shows. Every number goes into your station log, and you’ll need it for the council. Press Listen.

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: What will convince her?
parts.body: Then present your evidence to the council.

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
You have four clues. Crack the case, then stand up in front of the council and answer Councilor Ruiz.

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Then write your case report: two short answers, two station reports and your CER. Press Listen.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The claim
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “You can’t really prove that energy moved. You just have to trust it.”

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.

evidence.script:
[ON SCREEN: The claim]
Just trust it? Hmm. Think about your thermometer and your rice ruler.

There’s no wrong side, as long as you prove it.

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Tap your side and two facts, then explain how they prove your claim. Try starting with “This shows that…” Press Listen.

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 📋 Your specimen
parts.title: The approved work order
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

parts.label: ➡ Next week
parts.title: What happens when objects collide?
parts.body: Crashes, bumps and where the energy goes.

closing.script:
[ON SCREEN: A real lightning rod]
Case closed! Your evidence got the pier its lightning rod, just like this one.

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist, and the approved work order goes in your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Next week]
Next week, things start crashing! Press Listen for Sam’s last word.

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.
